correspondence.finding: The chosen northeastern opening, short western lead and long southwestward first part lie within the original map's Inland Ice terrain east of the coastal exposed-rock belt. Its complete interval was read. Ice-thickness shading and surface/bedrock contours are geographic context, not river-channel evidence.

The southward, slightly southwestward sequence remains within the broad mapped ice sheet. Every intermediate stored part and join is covered. The final bend enters the westward lower-ice approach; the original supplies no named natural-river line or selected lake passage here.

The numerous short westward parts and small southern steps cross the lower Inland Ice toward the coastal bedrock margin east of Jakobshavn Isfjord. The continuous mapped ice setting accounts for all intervals and joins at ordinary geographic scale. No separate-basin transfer or serial lake connection is inferred, and the contour and isopach lines are not interpreted as watercourses.

The lower western sequence reaches the pale ice-margin corridor between exposed-rock masses bordering the inner Jakobshavn Isfjord setting. Original clean pixels expose the full approach and its transition toward the historical fjord-side margin. National-map scale and epoch do not establish a precise current glacier front or an ordinary river mouth.

correspondence.component_scope: historical inner fjord and separate endings
correspondence.finding: The last westward bends and final short southward rendered part occupy the generalized historical inner Jakobshavn Isfjord setting west of the mapped lower-ice approach, with exposed rock to the north and south. The printed fjord label, surrounding margin and both separately supplied ending positions were read. The source position is slightly northwest of the rendered position, and the rendered final extension runs southward in the same inner-fjord setting. These do not establish a river channel, current ice/water boundary or current hydraulic connection.
correspondence.source_endpoint_description: The separately supplied source ending lies slightly northwest of the displayed ending in the historical inner Jakobshavn Isfjord setting; no surveyed mouth or present-day physical terminal class is asserted.
correspondence.render_endpoint_description: The displayed ending is slightly southeast of the source ending, after the short final southward extension, within the same ordinary historical inner-fjord setting.

correspondence.component_scope: Chosen western drainage south of Katy, through the Little Prong corridor
correspondence.finding: The actual chosen opening lies in the mapped minor-drainage network near the Crossover Road setting. The regional and upper originals show its south/east receiving corridor through developed land into the channel labeled Little Prong. The headmost connector has no separately supported hydronym; Little Prong is not promoted to the name of the entire system. Local road and development offsets do not establish a separate basin or require an exact channel alignment.

correspondence.component_scope: Northeast turn and upper Buffalo Bayou joining setting west of Grand Parkway
correspondence.finding: The Little Prong receiving corridor turns northeast toward the channel mapped and repeatedly labeled Buffalo Bayou near Grand Parkway. The larger northwestern Buffalo/Willow Fork approach is a separate incoming reach, not the selected opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Grand Parkway crossing and eastward entry into the Barker receiving floor
correspondence.finding: The mapped Buffalo Bayou continues east through the developed western margin and into the broad wetland/reservoir floor enclosed by Barker Dam. Small artificial ponds and side drains do not replace the through-going receiving corridor.

correspondence.component_scope: Barker Reservoir interior, northward bend and Mason Creek joining setting
correspondence.finding: Buffalo Bayou is mapped across the southern reservoir interior, turns northeast and receives the separately labeled Mason Creek from the northwest. The continuous managed receiving floor and mapped bayou lead onward toward the reservoir outlet. This is ordinary geographic passage through the impoundment setting, without claims about present impounded water, release rates or gate operation.

correspondence.component_scope: Barker outlet, Highway 6 and northern Addicks-side drainage contribution
correspondence.finding: The selected route reaches the eastern Barker Dam/outlet setting, passes into the downstream Buffalo Bayou corridor and receives the north-side drainage from the Addicks setting before continuing east. Addicks Reservoir itself is north of the selected mainstem and is not a selected lake crossing or an alias of Barker.

correspondence.component_scope: Western Houston and suburban Buffalo Bayou bends
correspondence.finding: The selected sequence follows the continuous named Buffalo Bayou through the western developed corridor, the southern bend by the Memorial/Bunker Hill/Piney Point surroundings and the northward turn toward the Memorial corridor. Regional and detailed views retain the same receiving channel despite simplified selected bends.

correspondence.component_scope: Memorial corridor, central Houston and Whiteoak Bayou joining setting
correspondence.finding: The repeatedly labeled Buffalo Bayou continues east through the Memorial green corridor into central Houston. The northern Whiteoak Bayou joins near the downtown end of this interval. It is a contextual tributary, not a selected modeled tributary or whole-system alias.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastward urban bayou and southeast turn toward Harrisburg
correspondence.finding: The mapped Buffalo Bayou remains continuous east of downtown, passes the mapped bend/cutoff surroundings and widens southeast toward Harrisburg. The selection stays on the receiving trunk rather than the northern tributary network.

correspondence.component_scope: Brays Bayou joining setting and eastward industrial-channel turn
correspondence.finding: Brays Bayou enters the broad Buffalo receiving corridor from the southwest near Harrisburg. The selected trunk turns east through the industrial waterfront and upper-channel widening. Brays is not part of the chosen opening.

correspondence.component_scope: Sims Bayou mouth and lower industrial corridor
correspondence.finding: The selected receiving trunk bends northeast beyond the southern Sims Bayou joining setting. Map labels continue to identify Buffalo Bayou on the broad industrial channel. No present navigation dimensions or operating condition are inferred.

correspondence.component_scope: Vince Bayou contribution and Galena Park-side receiving reach
correspondence.finding: The short stored parts occupy the continuous lower Buffalo corridor beside the industrial waterfront, with Vince Bayou mapped as a southern side entry. They are preserved as separate stored parts and are not interpreted as separate rivers.

correspondence.component_scope: Northward bend, Hunting Bayou and Greens Bayou joining settings
correspondence.finding: The broad receiving channel turns north and east. Hunting Bayou enters from the north near the western end and Greens Bayou enters farther east. Both entries are directly mapped; neither is a whole-system alias or an additional selected fragment.

correspondence.component_scope: Eastern channel bend and Deer Park-side lower reach
correspondence.finding: The named broad Buffalo Bayou corridor bends southeast and then east past the industrial shoreline, minor southern side channels and the Patrick Bayou vicinity. The channel continues toward the San Jacinto receiving setting. Exact docks, banks and current channel lines are outside this finding.

correspondence.component_scope: Lower Buffalo/San Jacinto receiving setting and Brownwood-side rendered ending
correspondence.finding: The lower map shows continuous receiving water from the eastern Buffalo Bayou channel to the Lynchburg Ferry/San Jacinto mouth setting and around the intervening peninsula into the Brownwood-side tidal water. The stored source endpoint is near Lynchburg Ferry, while the rendered endpoint is farther southeast at the mapped Brownwood shoreline setting. The straight final rendered extension crosses intervening land and shoreline; it is not asserted to be an all-water channel. Ordinary common receiving-setting correspondence is established, with no extension to an outer Galveston Bay or Gulf mouth.
The chosen western opening is on a small highland drainage corridor near residual snow patches. It continues east along a shallow valley before joining the north-trending valley.
The selected northward corridor receives side gullies and reaches the broad east-trending canyon at the bend. Original imagery shows a common receiving floor through the turn.
Long eastward incised valley beneath plateau margins, with successive north- and south-side tributary fans. The receiving valley is continuous through every short stored part.

Southeasterly bend and eastward continuation through the confined pale-rock valley. Side fans locally push the braided river across the common valley floor. Scotter’s independently located Mala valley field site corroborates this named corridor.
The valley opens onto lower tundra terrain and receives the northern tributary valley. The broad braided and alluvial corridor continues east through the selected lower parts toward the coast.

The selected ending lies in the broad southern part of the alluvial/deltaic coastal floor entering Navy Board Inlet. The stored source endpoint and slightly more easterly/southerly rendered ending occupy the same receiving setting and are described separately.
correspondence.scope_limit: No claim that either selected point equals the current wet-thread mouth; ordinary delta/shore correspondence is sufficient.

correspondence.finding: The chosen western opening is within continuous snow/ice terrain. The selected northeastward arc reaches the ice-covered passage at the northern end of a nunatak/ridge chain.

Eastward snow/ice passage around exposed peaks joins the larger north–south glacial valley. The original image shows uninterrupted ice terrain and the valley receiving relationship; present subglacial drainage is not inferred.

The selection follows the south-trending broad glacier beside the rock spine and bends east at its junction with the wider trunk. Visible glacier bands and common ice floor establish the ordinary transfer.

The widening trunk receives additional ice from the south/west and curves northeast around the central rocky ridge before meeting the north-side glacier branch. Blue surface meltwater pools are visible within the ice, but no independently named lake passage is asserted.

After the northern ice-branch join, the common glacier turns southeast between mountain walls and widens toward its front. The study’s original labeled imagery identifies this lower outlet as Trinity Glacier.

The final stored part reaches the broad ice-front/ice-mélange receiving setting in inner Talbot Inlet. The rendered endpoint and the more southerly stored source endpoint are both separately retained within this ice-covered marine-front setting.
